title: permission_handler
objectives: Understand permission_handler via a real-life analogy
Request runtime permissions correctly on Android + iOS
Work with Android 13+ media + notification permissions

sections.markdown:
**Think of `permission_handler` as the concierge that goes downstairs + asks the OS for a key on your behalf.**

Permissions are a triangle: manifest declaration (you) + OS prompt (concierge) + user decision (guest). Miss one leg + you get silent failures.

- **Declare in manifest / Info.plist first** — the OS only shows prompts for permissions you've listed.
- **Check current state** — `Permission.camera.status` returns `granted / denied / restricted / limited / permanentlyDenied / provisional`.
- **Request if not granted** — one call shows the OS dialog.
- **`permanentlyDenied` on Android** — user tapped 'Don't ask again.' Future `request()` calls no-op. Only path is `openAppSettings`.
- **Explainer UI first** — a bespoke 'why we need X' screen BEFORE the OS prompt dramatically boosts acceptance rates.
- **Android 13+ split-media** — one permission for images, another for videos, another for audio. Old READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is deprecated.
- **Post-notification permission (Android 13+)** — apps must ask; older Android grants automatically.

**Why the plugin exists despite being 'just a wrapper':** each permission has platform-specific quirks (iOS 'Ask Every Time' for photos, Android 'While in Use' vs 'Precise location', tri-state 'limited' for photos). `permission_handler` normalizes them into one Dart API + handles the manifest declarations + edge cases across ~40 permission types.

**`permission_handler`** normalizes Android + iOS runtime permission APIs into a Dart interface. `Permission` enum (camera, location, storage, photos, contacts, calendar, microphone, sms, notification, bluetooth, ...); each has `status`, `request`, `shouldShowRequestRationale` (Android). `openAppSettings()` bounces to the platform Settings app. Handles Android 13+ granular media permissions + POST_NOTIFICATIONS + Android 12 Bluetooth split.

sections.markdown: ## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: No pre-prompt explainer.** Cold OS prompts get denied ~40 %+ of the time. A 30-word screen explaining WHY doubles acceptance.
**Mistake 2: Ignoring `permanentlyDenied`.** Calling `request()` after 'Don't ask again' silently no-ops. Detect + prompt user to open Settings.
**Mistake 3: Requesting on app startup.** All prompts at once = user overwhelmed + denies all. Request just-in-time when the feature is used.
**Mistake 4: Missing manifest / Info.plist entries.** Silent failure on iOS; runtime crash on Android. Add ALL the ones you'll ever request.
**Mistake 5: Handling `restricted` as denied.** On iOS, parental control / MDM blocks may set restricted; user CANNOT grant. Disable the feature gracefully.
**Mistake 6: Assuming location is one permission.** Android 12+ has Approximate vs Precise; Always vs While-in-use; Background is separate.
**Mistake 7: Skipping POST_NOTIFICATIONS on Android 13+.** No FCM notifications appear; older Android auto-granted so devs forget.
**Mistake 8: Not handling `limited` photos (iOS 14+).** UI treats it as denied → user sees 'permission denied' when they DID grant a subset. Support limited mode.
## Best practices
**1. Pre-prompt explainer** before every non-trivial permission.
**2. Just-in-time** — request when the feature is used, not at launch.
**3. `openAppSettings` fallback** for permanentlyDenied.
**4. Batched requests** for tightly-coupled features (camera + mic for video).
**5. Analytics on decision** — grant / deny / open settings — learn your permission funnel.
**6. Support `limited` + `provisional` + `restricted` states**, not just denied/granted.
**7. React to Settings changes** — user may enable while app is background; re-check on resume.
**8. Test permission-denied paths** — feature should degrade gracefully, not crash.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Camera permission request with pre-prompt explainer.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Handle permanentlyDenied via `openAppSettings`.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Batched request (camera + mic) for video-calling flow.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — iOS 14+ limited-photos support: partial access UI.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS gated FCM enablement.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Permission funnel analytics + measure grant-rate delta from adding explainer.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: What's the difference between `denied` and `permanentlyDenied`?**

**A:** **`denied`** = the user hasn't decided yet OR denied once but didn't check 'Don't ask again.' A `request()` will show the OS prompt. **`permanentlyDenied`** = on Android, user tapped 'Don't ask again' at the OS prompt (or admin policy blocks). Future `request()` calls are NO-OPS — the OS won't re-prompt. The only recovery is calling `openAppSettings()` to bounce the user into iOS/Android Settings, where they toggle the permission manually. iOS analog: after the second denial, the OS remembers + won't show the system prompt again. **UX:** on `permanentlyDenied`, show an explicit dialog: 'Please enable Camera in Settings.' Deep-link to the specific settings page via `openAppSettings`.

**Q2: Why show a pre-prompt explainer before the OS prompt?**

**A:** Cold OS prompts get denied ~40 % of the time — the user has no context for why the app suddenly wants access. A **30-word Flutter screen** first ('We use your camera to scan barcodes — no photos saved') gives context AND lets the user opt out BEFORE hitting the OS prompt. If they say 'Not now,' the OS prompt never fires — the counter of denials doesn't tick up (crucial for Android's 'Don't ask again' flow). If they say 'Continue,' the OS prompt appears with the user already primed to accept. **Real-world measurement:** adding a good pre-prompt commonly moves grant rate from ~55 % → ~85 %. Google + Meta both recommend this pattern in their permission guidelines. Analytics: log 'shown / continued / declined / OS-granted / OS-denied' — you'll see the funnel + tune the copy.

**Q3: What changed with Android 13+ media permissions?**

**A:** Pre-Android 13, `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` granted access to the whole media store. On Android 13+, it's **split into 3 granular permissions**: `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES`, `READ_MEDIA_VIDEO`, `READ_MEDIA_AUDIO`. Request only what you need — an image-only app should NOT request audio. **In `permission_handler`,** `Permission.photos` maps to `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES` on Android 13+. **Android 14+** added **partial access** (like iOS 14+ limited photos) — user grants access to a subset via the system picker. **Best practice:** unless you MUST enumerate the library (rare), skip these permissions entirely + use the Android Photo Picker via `image_picker` — no permission needed for pick-only. **Interview highlight:** knowing 'you often don't need the permission at all' is the senior answer.

**Q4: Location permissions have three axes on Android — walk through them.**

**A:** **(1) Accuracy** — `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` (GPS-precise) vs `ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION` (network-cell-precise ~200 m). Android 12+ user can grant COARSE even if you request FINE. **(2) Lifecycle** — `WhileUsing` (foreground only) vs Always. Android 10+ requires `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` as a separate permission grant; user goes to Settings to allow. **(3) Precise vs Approximate toggle** — Android 12+ user can toggle precision even after grant. **In `permission_handler`:** `Permission.location`, `Permission.locationAlways`, `Permission.locationWhenInUse` — request in sequence: When-in-use first, then Always if truly needed. **UX:** never request Always up-front; earn trust with When-in-use first. iOS analog: `whileInUse` first; user upgrades to `always` in Settings via `openAppSettings`. **The 3-axis grid is a common interview question — knowing all three signals senior-level familiarity.**

**Q5: How do you handle `limited` (iOS 14+ photos)?**

**A:** iOS 14+ introduced `PHAuthorizationStatus.limited` — user grants access to a **subset** of photos via a system picker. Treating limited as denied breaks the UX; treating as granted breaks queries that return only the subset. **Best practice:** if `Permission.photos.request()` returns `.limited`, the app has access but may only see selected photos. `photo_manager` / `image_picker` handle this transparently for their APIs. If you must enumerate: (1) call `PHPhotoLibrary.presentLimitedLibraryPicker(from:)` to let the user add more selected photos (via `photo_manager` package). (2) show UI 'You've shared X photos. [Add more]' — respects their consent. **Trap:** iOS 15+ apps that don't handle `.limited` may be flagged by Apple in App Review. **Interview highlight:** mentioning limited by name is a differentiator.

**Q6: How do you test permission-dependent code?**

**A:** **Don't test the OS permission dialog.** Instead: **(1) Wrap the permission call in a `PermissionsGateway` interface**; production impl uses `permission_handler`. **(2) In tests, inject a fake gateway that returns pre-programmed `PermissionStatus` values.** Assert on business logic (denied → show explainer; granted → open scanner). **(3) Widget tests** use `permission_handler`'s `PermissionActions` test doubles (via method channel mocks). **(4) Integration tests on device:** manually grant + revoke; `patrol` package can drive the OS dialog. **(5) Analytics-driven test:** if you log permission decisions, verify the funnel events fire in expected sequence. **Interview signal:** 'we abstract behind an interface' is the target answer; anything mentioning method-channel mocks shows deeper knowledge.

## Real-world usage

- **Every app that reads camera / location / photos / mic** — foundational.
- **Notification opt-in** — Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS gates FCM.
- **Video calling** — camera + mic batched.
- **BLE apps** — Android 12+ Bluetooth split.
- **NOT for** — desktop / Web (fewer runtime permissions; simpler).

## Advanced notes

- **`shouldShowRequestRationale`** (Android) — hints whether to show explainer before request.
- **`openAppSettings(section: AppSettingsType.notification)`** — deep-link to specific settings page (some plugin versions).
- **App Setup Wizard** — some enterprise apps run a permission-onboarding sequence at first launch; wire analytics.
- **Permission funnel dashboard** — Firebase Analytics events: `permission_shown` / `permission_granted` / `permission_denied` — one row per permission.
- **Runtime permission changes** — user can revoke while app is running; re-check on resume via `AppLifecycleState.resumed`.
- **Precise vs Approximate location toggle** on Android 12+ — surface UI when precision drops.
- **MDM restrictions** — enterprise devices may deny app-level; can't override — detect + inform.
- **iOS `restricted`** — parental controls + Screen Time; treat as unrecoverable denial.
- **Notification permission is 'push' not 'local'** — local notifications still work on Android 12- without POST_NOTIFICATIONS; Android 13+ requires it for all.
- **Nearby Wi-Fi / Bluetooth Scan** — Android 12+ split; wire them individually.
- **Health data (HealthKit / Health Connect)** — separate SDKs with their own permission dance; `permission_handler` doesn't cover.
- **Motion & fitness** — iOS `NSMotionUsageDescription`; Android auto-granted.
